lesson.title: The Real Scale of the Solar System
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: Textbook pictures of the solar system are seriously misleading — the real distances between planets are far larger than any diagram can show to scale.

If the sun were shrunk to the size of a basketball (about 24 cm across), Earth would be about the size of a peppercorn, roughly 26 meters away — nearly the length of an Olympic swimming pool. On this same scale, Pluto would be over a kilometer away. This is why solar system diagrams in books always show planets close together — showing the real distances to scale would make the page impossibly wide. Using string or footsteps, try laying out this scale model at home: mark the 'sun' and pace out roughly 26 meters (or a smaller fraction, like 2.6 meters, if space is limited) to place 'Earth.'
You just experienced the real, surprising scale of the solar system firsthand. Tomorrow we'll review everything about space systems from this whole week.

objectives: Explain why textbook solar system diagrams are not drawn to scale
Build or estimate a real-scale distance model between the sun and Earth
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child if they've ever noticed solar system pictures show planets close together.
2. Introduce the basketball-sun/peppercorn-Earth scale model.
3. If space allows, physically pace out the scaled distance together.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on the single striking fact (26 meters away on this scale) rather than requiring the child to do the full physical pacing
Ready for more: research how far Pluto would be on this same scale and compare it to Earth's distance
The physical pacing-out activity, even indoors at a smaller fraction of scale, makes the abstract distance genuinely felt rather than just stated
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. On a basketball-sized sun, Earth would be about 26 meters away. 2. Diagrams aren't drawn to scale because real distances are far too large to fit on a page. 3. Answers will vary for the child's own scale-model activity.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS MS-ESS1-3: analyzing and interpreting data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system, using a real, hands-on scale-model activity rather than abstract numbers alone.
